name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.97.0 — sketch owns high fidelity and closes with a fixed critique pass (brief 22a): `/spec:sketch`'s scoped sweep now authors every gap surface at production fidelity in the picked theme and reworks the brief's existing gray mocks into it (the one re-authoring exception), and its loop writes a three-line UX argument (`job:`/`risk:`/`choice:`) into the brief's `surfaces` block per surface touched; a new fixed step runs `check --states`, `render-gate --mocks`, and one fresh-context `design-critic` (Opus, read-only) dispatch on the four blind spots (error prevention · error recovery · help · efficiency) before every exit stop, recording findings as page notes (`notes add --by critic --reason <blindspot>`); `design-atlas.js check` gains two stamp-bound violations — a labeled mock still linking `wire/` once `design/tokens.css` exists (violation at `ratified`, warn at `sketch`, `approved` wireframes exempt) and a `ratified` mock with unresolved critic/human notes on its own label — both byte-identical no-ops when their store is absent; `mocks-notes.js`'s reason enum gains the four blind spots and `notes add`/`notes open` carry them. 7.96.0 — gray states on every wireframe (brief 22a): `design-atlas.js check --states` requires every labeled non-canon mock to declare `data-state-btn` switches for `empty`, `loading`, and `error` alongside the happy path, or opt one out with `data-no-state="<name>[,<name>]"` on the labeled root naming a product reason recorded as a ledger row; `mocks-driver.js` runs the check at `journey-drawn` and `journey-approved`, refusing the mark with the missing states named and the remedy to redraw them; `render-gate --mocks` captures every declared state as before, so the empty/loading/error frames join the render matrix with no gate change; the mocks-driver test fixture's `writeWireframe` now draws all three states by default. 7.95.0 — the journey review page (brief 22a): `stop open journey:<j>` now points at `/review/<j>.html`, a derived three-pane page (screens rail, per-screen artboards with `happy|empty|loading|error` state tabs at `?state=<s>` on the served mock, and a question/note inspector answered in place with `J K Y N Esc \`) built by the new `lib/review-page.js`/`lib/review.browser.js` and routed through `design-atlas.js`; the approve control mirrors the on-disk gate, disabled while any question or note is open; `shapes`/`theme`/`signoff`/`variants:<j>` stops keep the atlas URL. Plugin chrome (atlas, review page, galleries, notes layer) is now one doctrine home, design.md § Design Canon, authored under the frontend-design skill in the shadcn idiom on viewer.css's register. Fixes the atlas's frame-height floor: a viewport-filling mock (`100vh` app shells, sign-in screens) measured its `scrollHeight` before the iframe reached its declared height and rendered as a squashed ~150px strip; every card and artboard iframe now carries `width`+`height` from the primary viewport before measurement.
